styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old Town lanes, sulphur baths and the best of the city's museums.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Khinkali, khachapuri and long wine-filled dinners.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Churches, fortresses and the layers of an old Silk Road city.

stays.why: Walk to the sulphur baths, Narikala and the main lanes. Lively but can be noisy at night.
Central and well connected: metro, museums and the main avenue on your doorstep.
Quieter, local feel with cafés and bars; a short walk or cheap ride to the centre.
Historic streets with old balconies, between Freedom Square and the Old Town.

food: Try khinkali (dumplings) and khachapuri (cheese bread). Eat khinkali by hand, hold the top knot and sip the juice first.
Book a long dinner: Georgian tables fill with plates to share. Expect GEL 30–70 per person without much wine.
Wine is the local pride. Ask for qvevri (clay-jar) wines by the glass; a good bottle is often GEL 25–60 in a restaurant.
Cheap eats: bakeries sell fresh khachapuri and lobiani for a few GEL. Street food and small cafeterias keep meals under GEL 15.
Vegetarians do well: lobio (beans), badrijani (aubergine rolls) and pkhali (walnut vegetable pâtés) are everywhere.
more_time: Swap a city day for Mtskheta, the old capital: about 30 minutes by marshrutka or taxi, with the Jvari church viewpoint.
Add a day trip to the Kakheti wine region (Sighnaghi, Telavi). Go with a driver or tour so you can taste wine safely.
Take the cable car up to Narikala and walk down through the Old Town; finish at the sulphur baths in Abanotubani.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Old Town, the main museums and a long food-and-wine evening, with time for one day trip.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 6°C and lows around -2°C. Pack a warm coat; some rain days.
February: still cold, highs near 8°C. Quiet season with lower prices.
March: warming to about 11°C but the wettest month, with around 12 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
April: mild at 17°C with 12 rain days. Good for walking between showers.
May: pleasant at 21°C, but around 14 rain days — the wettest stretch. Keep plans flexible.
June: warm at 27°C with fewer rain days. Long evenings outdoors.
July: hot, highs near 30°C. Do sights early and rest in the afternoon.
August: hot like July, around 30°C. Shade and water matter.
September: warm and drier, highs near 25°C. One of the best months to visit.
October: mild at 17°C with 9 rain days. Good for city walks and day trips.
November: cooler at 11°C with 6 rain days. Bring layers.
December: cold, highs near 7°C and lows near 0°C. Festive lights in the centre.

climate_guide.summary: Tbilisi has four clear seasons: cold winters, mild springs, hot dry-ish summers and a warm, pleasant autumn.

items.title: Best months: May, September and October
items.text: Mild to warm days around 17–25°C. September is warm and drier than spring.

items.title: Hot summer (July–August)
items.text: Highs near 30°C. Sightsee in the morning, then rest or stay indoors in the afternoon.

items.title: Wettest in spring
items.text: March, April and May have the most rain days (12–14). Carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Cold winter (December–February)
items.text: Highs of 6–8°C and lows near or below freezing. A warm coat and shoes are essential.

items.title: Autumn is a sweet spot
items.text: September and October are warm and drier, with 7–9 rain days. Great for walking and day trips.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for spring and autumn, a warm coat for winter, and light clothes plus sun protection for summer. Good walking shoes for uneven pavements.

transit.best: Walk the centre; use the metro for longer hops and ride apps for late nights.

modes.text: Two lines cover the centre and main sights. Buy a Metromoney card at stations.
Buses and marshrutkas reach most of the city. Pay with the card or contactless.
Bolt and Yandex Go work well and are usually cheaper than street taxis. Street taxis often quote high — agree the price first or use an app.
Driving is chaotic. Most visitors skip renting a car in town.
The centre is walkable, but pavements are uneven, so wear good shoes.
